proposals.impact: removes zero-start rate blocking all quiz funnel data
proposals.observation: The quiz had 1 session load the intro screen and 0 starts in 48 hours. No one pressed the begin button. The "Quiz Events" GitHub workflow failed twice yesterday (15:53 and 17:57 UTC), which suggests the event-tracking script may be throwing an error that blocks the start interaction entirely. The intro loads — the JavaScript breaks before the first click registers.
proposals.proposal: Check QuizIntro.astro for an event listener or fetch call that runs on page load and throws before the start button becomes interactive. The two timed failures (two hours apart, same workflow) point to a runtime error rather than a flaky network call. Look for an uncaught promise on the analytics ping — if it rejects, it likely prevents the button's onClick from binding. Add a try/catch around the analytics initialisation so a tracking failure cannot block the user action. This is the highest-leverage fix in the batch: every other funnel metric is zero because no one can get past step one.

proposals.impact: converts 66% open rate into discovery call clicks
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sends — the strongest engagement signal in the whole dataset. The Money Avoidance sequence opens at 52.63% and Money Worship at 37.5%. None of the automation files are in the blocked-paths list. The vigilance audience is reading. The question is whether email 1 gives them somewhere to go.
proposals.proposal: Add a single, direct call-to-action at the close of the first Money Vigilance email pointing to the discovery call booking page. The existing close almost certainly ends on an observation about vigilance patterns with no next step — which means the 66% who open read, feel seen, and close the tab. One sentence and a plain URL is enough. Keep the tone consistent with the email: grounded, specific, no pressure framing.

proposals.impact: fills content gap while Daily Blog Post workflow is broken
proposals.observation: The content queue shows 1 post queued and 47 published. The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at 06:04 UTC yesterday and has not recovered — no commits in the last 24 hours confirm nothing published automatically. The three most recent posts all date from June 2026, which means the queue has been stalled for weeks. There is one post sitting ready. It will not publish itself while the workflow is broken.
proposals.proposal: Manually set the queued post's pubDate to today (2026-08-07) and push it directly. This bypasses the broken Daily Blog Post workflow without touching .github/workflows/ (which is blocked). The post reaches the audience, the content gap closes, and Joel gets a live signal on whether the workflow failure is a scheduling issue or something deeper in the build. Title the commit clearly so the failure pattern is easy to spot in the run history.
